chapters.reason: The paper directly introduces Liger, a method for converting pretrained LLMs into linear recurrent structures, which matches the description of linearization as converting pretrained transformers to linear RNNs without extensive retraining.
Liger replaces standard self-attention with linear recurrent modeling to achieve subquadratic complexity, aligning with the focus on mechanisms that reduce quadratic complexity in transformers.

The paper evaluates Liger on reasoning benchmarks, showing it recovers 93% of Transformer performance, indicating an application of subquadratic attention models to reasoning tasks, though it is less central than the linearization conversion itself.
